title: Focus State
definition: A state variant (`focus:`) that applies a utility class ONLY when the element is currently selected/active (e.g., clicking into a text input, or tabbing to a button via keyboard).
simpleExplanation: When you click inside an email `<input>`, the border should turn blue so you know you are actively typing in it. This is crucial for users who navigate websites using the 'Tab' key instead of a mouse.
realWorldExample: Changing an input field from `border-gray-300` to `border-brand-500` the moment the user clicks into it to start typing.

basic: What prefix is used to change the background color of an input field when the user clicks into it?
intermediate: What is `focus-visible:` and why is it sometimes better than `focus:`?

answers.question: focus-visible?
answers.answer: `focus-visible:` ONLY applies the focus ring if the user navigated to the element using a Keyboard. It hides the focus ring if they clicked it with a Mouse. This prevents ugly blue rings from appearing when mouse users click buttons, while still protecting accessibility for keyboard users.

codeExample:
<!-- 
  A highly accessible, beautifully styled Input Field 
  1. Base: Gray border
  2. Focus: Removes default outline, turns border Blue, adds a Blue Ring
-->
<input 
  type="email" 
  placeholder="Email Address"
  class="border border-gray-300 rounded px-4 py-2 w-full 
         focus:outline-none focus:border-blue-500 focus:ring-1 focus:ring-blue-500" 
/>

<!-- Using focus-visible to keep mouse users happy -->
<button class="bg-blue-500 px-4 py-2 focus:outline-none focus-visible:ring-4 focus-visible:ring-blue-300">
  No ring when clicked! Ring appears when Tabbed to!
</button>
